questions.prompt: Coffee in a 20°C room has temperature T(t) = 20 + 70(0.95)^t °C after t minutes. What do 20 and 70(0.95)^t represent?
questions.prompt_markup: Coffee in a 20°C room has temperature T(t) = 20 + 70(0.95)^t °C after t minutes. What do 20 and 70(0.95)^t represent?

choices.text: 20 is the room temperature; 70(0.95)^t is how far the coffee is above room temperature, which shrinks 5% each minute.
20 is the starting temperature of the coffee; 70(0.95)^t is the room temperature, which falls 5% each minute.
20 is the number of minutes the coffee cools; 70(0.95)^t is the temperature of the coffee at time t.
20 is the room temperature; 70(0.95)^t is the drop in the coffee's temperature during each minute.

questions.correct_answer: 20 is the room temperature; 70(0.95)^t is how far the coffee is above room temperature, which shrinks 5% each minute.
questions.grading_note: T approaches 20 as the second term decays. The others swap the parts (T(0) = 90), misread 20, or confuse the remaining difference with the drop.

questions.prompt: A town has P(t) = 5000(1.02)^t people and F(t) = 6000 + 100t units of food after t years. Why does the food per person F(t)/P(t) eventually decrease?
questions.prompt_markup: A town has P(t) = 5000(1.02)^t people and F(t) = 6000 + 100t units of food after t years. Why does the food per person F(t)/P(t) eventually decrease?

choices.text: F(t)/P(t) is constant because both F and P increase every year, so their ratio does not change as time passes.
P(t) = 5000(1.02)^t decreases over time, so there are fewer people for the same food.
F(t) = 6000 + 100t decreases over time, so there is less food for the same number of people.
P grows exponentially (factor 1.02 each year) while F grows linearly, so P eventually grows much faster.

questions.correct_answer: P grows exponentially (factor 1.02 each year) while F grows linearly, so P eventually grows much faster.
questions.grading_note: Exponential growth with a factor greater than 1 eventually outpaces any linear growth. The others contradict the formulas.

questions.prompt: How does composing two functions differ from multiplying them?
questions.prompt_markup: How does composing two functions differ from multiplying them?

choices.text: Composition f(g(x)) adds the two outputs f(x) + g(x); multiplication f(x) · g(x) multiplies them.
Composition f(g(x)) uses the output of g as the input of f; multiplication f(x) · g(x) multiplies the two outputs.
Composition f(g(x)) multiplies the inputs of f and g; multiplication f(x) · g(x) multiplies the outputs.
They are the same operation written two ways: f(g(x)) and f(x) · g(x) are always equal.

questions.correct_answer: Composition f(g(x)) uses the output of g as the input of f; multiplication f(x) · g(x) multiplies the two outputs.
questions.grading_note: For f(x) = x + 1 and g(x) = 2x: f(g(x)) = 2x + 1, but f(x)g(x) = 2x² + 2x. The others say composition adds outputs or multiplies inputs, or claim the two operations are the same.
